info.title: Parallax API
info.description: Parallax by Chicago Global — AI-powered investment research and portfolio analytics. Multi-factor scoring, portfolio analysis and tracking, financial statements, analyst estimates, ETF analytics, valuation (DCF & multiples), macro and market telemetry, and AI-generated research reports. Credits can be fractional. Per-symbol reads cost 0.05 credits per submitted symbol; see each operation for its price. A 503 indicates an availability failure, not data age.

post.description:
Generate comprehensive stock report (ASYNC - returns job_id immediately).

This endpoint creates a background job for report generation. The actual generation
happens asynchronously without blocking. Use GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} to check status.

**Response Format:**
```json
{
    "job_id": "uuid-string",
    "status": "pending",
    "symbol": "AAPL.O",
    "check_url": "/v1/jobs/{job_id}",
    "estimated_duration_seconds": 300
}
```

**Workflow:**
1. POST /stock-report → Get job_id (returns in <1 second)
2. Poll GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} every 5-10 seconds
3. When status="completed", result contains pdf_url, html_url, json_url

**Example:**
```bash
# Start generation
curl -X POST "https://api.chicago.global/v1/stock-report" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key" \
     -d '{"symbol":"AAPL.O","force":false}'

# Check status
curl "https://api.chicago.global/v1/jobs/{job_id}" -H "Authorization: Bearer key"
```

**Credits:** 10 credits per job. Charged when the job completes successfully. Polling is free.

get.description:
Get status of a background job.

Use this endpoint to check the status of long-running operations like:
- Stock report generation (/stock-report)
- Score analysis (/v1/score-analysis)
- News analysis (/v1/news-analysis)
- Financial analysis (/v1/financial-analysis)

Status values:
- pending: Job created, not started yet
- processing: Job is currently running (check 'progress' field for details)
- completed: Job finished successfully (result contains the data)
- failed: Job failed (error contains the error message)

Example:
    POST /v1/stock-report -> {"job_id": "abc-123", "status": "pending"}
    GET /v1/jobs/abc-123 -> {"status": "processing", "progress": "Generating PDF..."}
    GET /v1/jobs/abc-123 -> {"status": "completed", "result": {...}}

**Credits:** Free (0 credits).

post.description:
Analyze a portfolio with multi-currency support, rebalancing, and comprehensive metrics (ASYNC - returns job_id immediately).

This endpoint creates a background job for portfolio analysis. The actual analysis
happens asynchronously without blocking. Use GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} to check status.

**Response Format:**
```json
{
    "job_id": "uuid-string",
    "status": "pending",
    "check_url": "/v1/jobs/{job_id}",
    "estimated_duration_seconds": 90
}
```

**Workflow:**
1. POST /portfolio/analyze -> Get job_id (returns in <1 second)
2. Poll GET /v1/jobs/{job_id} every 3-5 seconds
3. When status="completed", result contains full analysis

**Portfolio Analysis Includes:**
- Performance metrics (returns, Sharpe, Sortino, etc.)
- Risk metrics (volatility, drawdown, VaR, etc.)
- Attribution analysis (by security, sector, market, currency)
- Rolling metrics (30/60/90-day windows)
- Benchmark comparison
- Transaction history and rebalancing details

**Portfolio Format:**
- Each holding requires: date, symbol, and weight (as decimal)
- Weights should sum to 1.0 for each date
- Multiple dates can be provided for rebalancing

**Field Selection (Optional):**
Use the `fields` parameter to return only specific data sections. If omitted, all fields are returned.

Available fields: `portfolio_parameters`, `portfolio_input`, `data_quality`, `portfolio_summary`,
`performance_metrics`, `rolling_metrics`, `drawdown_analysis`, `portfolio_scores`, `concentration_metrics`,
`transactions`, `company_info`, `latest_holdings`, `market_allocation`, `sector_allocation`,
`currency_allocation`, `company_contribution`, `sector_contribution`, `market_contribution`,
`time_period_returns`, `monthly_returns`, `annual_returns`, `daily_summary`.

**Example Request:**
```json
{
  "start_date": "2024-01-01",
  "end_date": "2024-11-01",
  "base_currency": "USD",
  "benchmark": "SPY",
  "initial_value": 10000,
  "portfolio": [
    {"date": "2024-01-01", "symbol": "AAPL", "weight": 0.25},
    {"date": "2024-01-01", "symbol": "MSFT", "weight": 0.25},
    {"date": "2024-01-01", "symbol": "GOOGL", "weight": 0.25},
    {"date": "2024-01-01", "symbol": "AMZN", "weight": 0.25}
  ],
  "fields": ["portfolio_summary", "performance_metrics", "latest_holdings"]
}
```

**Example:**
```bash
# Start analysis
curl -X POST "https://api.chicago.global/v1/portfolio/analyze" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key" \
     -d '{"start_date":"2024-01-01",...}'

# Check status
curl "https://api.chicago.global/v1/jobs/{job_id}" -H "Authorization: Bearer key"
```

**Credits:** 5 credits per job. Charged when the job completes successfully. Polling is free.

post.description:
Dry-run validation for a new portfolio definition (same body as /track).

Returns every validation error and warning without persisting anything.
Use this client-side before calling /track to fix all issues in one pass.

**Credits:** Free (0 credits).

Resolve a portfolio definition and validate the result.

Accepts the same body as /track. Normalizes symbols to RICs, removes unresolvable symbols and future-dated rows, deduplicates entries, removes non-positive weights, and renormalizes weights for each date to sum to 1.0. The result is checked with the same validator used by /track.

Returns HTTP 200 with one of three statuses without persisting changes:
- "clean": the input is valid and returned unchanged.
- "resolved": the returned portfolio contains the corrected definition for submission to /track.
- "unresolvable": the definition requires further changes; see validation.errors for details.

Review the changes and dropped entries before submitting the resolved portfolio.

**Credits:** Free (0 credits).

get.description:
Get every holding in the portfolio definition across all rebalance dates, with the submitted date, symbol, and weight. For the most recent computed holdings and drifted weights, use /holdings/latest.

**Credits:** Free (0 credits).

Get the latest computed holdings — the portfolio's current
state on its most recent computed day, with drifted weights / ending values.
For the as-defined definition (all rebalance dates) use /holdings.

Discriminated status, matching /analytics:
  - {status: "ready", holdings}   when the series is computed
  - {status: "not_computed", holdings: []} (200) when the portfolio exists but
    its series is empty (a background compute hasn't landed)
  - 404 only when the portfolio genuinely doesn't exist.

**Credits:** Free (0 credits).

post.description:
Target weights for 2 to 100 holdings under up to six schemes, side by side.

The weights describe the latest close in the data for these holdings, reported as `as_of`. Every scheme
reads the same risk window of `lookback_days` daily price returns in the base currency. Returns are price
returns, so dividends are not included. The output is a calculation, not investment advice.

- `equal_weight`: the same weight in every holding.
- `value_weight`: weights in proportion to market capitalisation. Long-only.
- `conviction`: weights in proportion to score, or score squared.
- `inverse_vol`: weights in proportion to 1 / volatility.
- `risk_parity`: every holding contributes its budgeted share of predicted risk. Long-only.
- `mean_variance`: the best trade-off between score-implied return and predicted risk, with at most
  `max_weight` in any holding.

With shorts, `equal_weight`, `conviction` and `inverse_vol` go long the higher-scored holdings and short
the others, and `mean_variance` solves both sides. Short positions pay no borrow fee and their proceeds
earn nothing.

A scheme that cannot run returns `status: failed` with a code and a message that says what to change; the
other schemes still return. A request that cannot be served is a 422 whose `detail` lists each problem as
`{code, message, ...}` with only the fields that apply, such as `holdings`: `unknown_symbols`,
`duplicate_holdings`, `no_recent_price`, `unsupported_base_currency`, `no_fx_for_holding`,
`scheme_not_available_in_mode`, `invalid_risk_budget`, `invalid_max_weight` or `all_schemes_failed`, which
carries every scheme's error.

Costs 1 credit, charged only when the response is a 200.

Simulate fixed and re-optimised portfolios over the same holdings, with rebalancing and trading costs.

Runs as a job. Poll `check_url` until `status` is `completed`; `result` then holds `start_date`,
`end_date`, `trading_days`, `base_currency`, `holdings` (each holding's first and last close in the
window), `portfolios` (metrics, the value series, every rebalance and the final weights; or, for a
re-optimised portfolio whose scheme could not run on a rebalance date, that date and the reason),
`benchmark` and `warnings`.

Each portfolio starts as 1.0 in cash, buys its targets at the first trade date's close and pays
`cost_bps` per side on the value traded. A fixed portfolio trades back to its weights on every rebalance
date. A re-optimised portfolio re-runs its scheme on each rebalance date with only the data available the
day before, as propose-weights would have answered that day. Values are price returns in the base
currency, so dividends are not included; cash and short-sale proceeds earn nothing and shorts pay no
borrow fee. The output is a simulation, not investment advice.

Every problem the caller can fix is a 422 before any job exists, with `detail` listing each problem as
`{code, message, ...}` with only the fields that apply, such as `holdings`, `portfolio` and
`earliest_start`: for example `unknown_symbols`,
`duplicate_holdings`, `invalid_weights`, `rebalance_required`, `window_too_short`, `window_too_long`,
`no_prices_in_window`, `stopped_trading`, `benchmark_no_prices`, `empty_leg_at_start` and
`not_computable_at_start`, which names the earliest workable start date.

Costs 2 credits, charged when the job completes. A 422 is not charged.

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.description: Tickers or RICs of listed stocks and funds, 2 to 100, for example AAPL, 7203.T or SPY. Each must resolve to a different listing. Weights come back keyed by these strings exactly as sent.

base_currency.title: Base Currency
base_currency.description: Currency of every price, return, volatility and market cap. Each close converts at its own day's exchange rate. Any currency with exchange rates works.

lookback_days.title: Lookback Days
lookback_days.description: Trading days of daily returns behind every risk estimate (756 is about three years). inverse_vol, risk_parity and mean_variance need each holding to have traded for the whole window.

portfolios.title: Portfolios
portfolios.description: 1 to 8 portfolios with unique names: fixed weights, or a scheme and mode re-run on every rebalance date.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: The backtest starts on the first trading day on or after this date. Default: 5 years before end_date.

end_date.title: End Date
end_date.description: The last day simulated. Default: the holdings' latest close before today.

rebalance.title: Rebalance
rebalance.description: How often portfolios trade back to their targets, on the last trading day of each month, quarter or year. Re-optimised portfolios need one other than none.

cost_bps.title: Cost Bps
cost_bps.description: Trading cost per side, in basis points of the value traded, including the first purchase.

benchmark.title: Benchmark
benchmark.description: A stock or fund bought and held over the same window, in the base currency, with the same metrics. No default.

timeseries.title: Timeseries
timeseries.description: Value series returned per portfolio: none, monthly (last day of each month) or daily.

BacktestWeightsRequest.title: BacktestWeightsRequest
BacktestWeightsRequest.description: Portfolios to simulate over the same holdings and window.

power.title: Power
power.description: Exponent on the score: 1 weights by score, 2 by score squared.

Conviction.title: Conviction
Conviction.description:
Weights in proportion to score (or score squared). In a long/short mode the top fifth
of holdings by score is long and the bottom fifth short, weighted by distance from the
median score.

EqualWeight.title: EqualWeight
EqualWeight.description:
Equal weights. In a long/short mode the higher-scored half of the holdings is long
and the rest short, equally weighted within each side.

message.title: Message
message.description: What failed and what to change.

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.description: Holdings involved, keyed by symbol, and why.

weights.title: Weights
weights.description: Target weight per holding, keyed by symbols in holdings; holdings left out are 0. Long-only weights sum to 1; with shorts, the sum is 1 or 0 and the sum of absolute weights is at most 2.

FixedPortfolio.title: FixedPortfolio
FixedPortfolio.description:
Fixed target weights, traded back to on every rebalance date. A holding without a local close
cannot trade: its position uses the last local close and the exchange rate available on the
valuation date. Executable targets are rescaled around those positions.

score.title: Score
score.description: Composite score from 0 to 10; null means no view.

score_date.title: Score Date
score_date.description: Date of the score; null when there is no score, and for a fund, whose score is current and undated.

volatility.title: Volatility
volatility.description: Annualised volatility of daily returns in the base currency over the lookback; null when the holding has not traded for the whole lookback.

InverseVol.title: InverseVol
InverseVol.description:
Weights in proportion to 1 / volatility. In a long/short mode holdings scored at or
above the median are long and the rest short, by 1 / volatility within each side.

max_weight.title: Max Weight
max_weight.description: Largest absolute weight any holding may take, at most the mode's long exposure (1 in long_only, 1.3 in 130_30, 1.5 in 150_50, 1 in dollar_neutral). Default: twice the holding's equal share of gross exposure, up to the long exposure (2 / N long-only, at most 1).

MeanVariance.title: MeanVariance
MeanVariance.description:
Long-only: the weights with the highest score-implied excess return per unit of predicted
volatility. Long/short: the best trade-off between that return and predicted variance.
Holdings without a score have no view (zero expected excess return).

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: The latest close used; the weights describe this date.

lookback.description: First and last date of the prices behind risk estimates.

risk_model.description: The shared risk estimate behind every predicted_volatility and risk_contributions. Null when a holding lacks the whole lookback or the estimate fails; a no_risk_estimate warning says why.

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.description: Tickers or RICs of listed stocks and funds, 2 to 100, for example AAPL, 7203.T or SPY. Each must resolve to a different listing. Weights come back keyed by these strings exactly as sent.

base_currency.title: Base Currency
base_currency.description: Currency of every price, return, volatility and market cap. Each close converts at its own day's exchange rate. Any currency with exchange rates works.

lookback_days.title: Lookback Days
lookback_days.description: Trading days of daily returns behind every risk estimate (756 is about three years). inverse_vol, risk_parity and mean_variance need each holding to have traded for the whole window.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Exposure, as a fraction of capital: long_only (100% long, 0% short), 130_30 (130% long, 30% short), 150_50 (150% long, 50% short), dollar_neutral (100% long, 100% short).

schemes.title: Schemes
schemes.description: Schemes to run, each at most once. Default: every scheme available in the mode, which is all six in long_only and equal_weight, conviction, inverse_vol and mean_variance with shorts.

ProposeWeightsRequest.title: ProposeWeightsRequest
ProposeWeightsRequest.description: Holdings to weight, the exposure, and the schemes to compare.

ReoptimisedPortfolio.title: ReoptimisedPortfolio
ReoptimisedPortfolio.description: A scheme re-run on every rebalance date with only the data available the day before.

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.description: no_risk_estimate: the holdings behind it, keyed by symbol, and why.

dropped_days.title: Dropped Days
dropped_days.description: Days left out because a holding had no price.

shrinkage.title: Shrinkage
shrinkage.description: Weight on the shrinkage target, from 0 to 1.

risk_budget.title: Risk Budget
risk_budget.description: Share of predicted risk per holding, keyed by the symbols in holdings. Every holding needs a positive value; values are rescaled to sum to 1. Omit for equal risk.

RiskParity.title: RiskParity
RiskParity.description:
Weights at which every holding contributes its budgeted share of predicted risk
(equal shares by default). Long-only and uncapped.

SchemeFailed.title: SchemeFailed
SchemeFailed.description: A scheme that could not produce weights; the other schemes are unaffected.

weights.title: Weights
weights.description: Target weight per holding; negative is short.

effective_holdings.title: Effective Holdings
effective_holdings.description: (sum of |w|)^2 / sum of w^2: how many equal positions would be as concentrated.

predicted_volatility.title: Predicted Volatility
predicted_volatility.description: Annualised volatility predicted for these weights; null when risk_model is null.

risk_contributions.title: Risk Contributions
risk_contributions.description: Share of predicted variance per holding; sums to 1. Null when risk_model is null.

max_weight.title: Max Weight
max_weight.description: mean_variance only: the largest absolute weight it allowed.

ValueWeight.title: ValueWeight
ValueWeight.description: Weights in proportion to market capitalisation in the base currency. Long-only.
